prerequisites: Knowledge of physical, data link, network, and transport layers of the OSI model

learning_outcomes.text: Know the methods of network routing and interconnection.
Design and develop network interconnection applications, as well as analyze and interpret their results.
Analyze and evaluate routing protocols using computer tools.
Create and use models of real networks using network simulators.
Use congestion control techniques to perform proper network planning and dimensioning.

syllabus_topics: Classification of congestion control methods, implicit and explicit congestion control, traffic modeling
Introduction to QoS concepts, Integrated Services, Differentiated Services
assessment_rules: In the ordinary and extraordinary calls, if all established minimums are reached, the final grade is calculated as: Final Grade = 0.7 x TE + 0.3 x PL. Both the theory exam and the laboratory practices must be passed with a minimum of 5 out of 10 points. If any part is not passed, the final grade will be 4.5 points. Grades for passed blocks are carried over between calls within the same academic year.
